findings.reason: The diff only edits decimal.d.ts:254 and decimal.global.d.ts:275. The package.json test script runs only `node ./test/test.js`, there is no tsconfig or type test, and test/modules/isFiniteEtc.js:261-277 asserts only runtime booleans. The gap is real. It stays low because the runtime implementation (decimal.js:4534 isDecimalInstance) is unchanged and already tested.
findings.claim: The new `object is Decimal` type guard isn't checked by anything in the repo, so a later regression wouldn't be caught.
findings.evidence: The diff only changes `static isDecimal(object: any): boolean` to `static isDecimal(object: any): object is Decimal;` in decimal.d.ts:254 and decimal.global.d.ts:275. The only tests (test/modules/isFiniteEtc.js:261-277) are runtime JS assertions such as `t(Decimal.isDecimal(new Decimal(1)))`, which pass whatever the .d.ts says. The export contains no tsconfig, no tsc step and no type test (for example, narrowing an `unknown` and calling a Decimal method).
